description: Transparent triage ruleset. Group caps sum to 100 so the score never needs clipping and one underlying pattern cannot be counted several times. v1.1 adds the shared contact + service overlap combination (collusion pattern without duplicate billing).

continuous_scoring.note: robust_z = (value - reference median) / (1.4826 * MAD). Points scale linearly from z_start (0 points) to z_full (full points). Reference = the loaded queue.

duplicate_service_billed.label: Duplicate service billed
duplicate_service_billed.why: The same service appears to be billed more than once.

service_overlap_other_provider.label: Service overlap with another provider
service_overlap_other_provider.why: Billed services overlap with services another provider billed for the same member.

shared_contact_with_provider.label: Shared contact info with provider
shared_contact_with_provider.why: Member and provider share contact details, which is unusual for an independent care relationship.

recent_policy_change_flag.label: Recent policy change
recent_policy_change_flag.why: The policy changed shortly before the claim. Weak on its own; often benign.

weekly_visit_frequency.label: Weekly visit frequency
weekly_visit_frequency.why: Visits per week are high relative to the queue.

member_provider_distance_miles.label: Member-provider distance
member_provider_distance_miles.why: The member lives far from the provider for recurring care.

prior_claims_last_12mo.label: Prior claims (12 months)
prior_claims_last_12mo.why: The member has many prior claims. Can also reflect genuine high care needs.

amount_vs_peer_avg_pct.label: Amount vs peer average
amount_vs_peer_avg_pct.why: The claim amount is well above the peer average for similar claims.

weekend_billing_ratio.label: Weekend billing ratio
weekend_billing_ratio.why: A high share of visits are billed on weekends.

round_dollar_billing_ratio.label: Round-dollar billing ratio
round_dollar_billing_ratio.why: Many line items are billed in round dollar amounts, a common sign of estimated rather than recorded billing.

combinations.label: Duplicate billing + service overlap
combinations.why: Duplicate billing alongside overlapping services from another provider is harder to explain than either alone.

combinations.label: Shared contact + duplicate billing
combinations.why: Shared contact details plus duplicate billing raises the possibility of a non-arm's-length relationship.

combinations.label: Shared contact + service overlap
combinations.why: Shared contact details together with services overlapping another provider's suggest a coordinated arrangement, even without duplicate billing.

combinations.label: High frequency + long distance
combinations.why: Frequent visits combined with long travel distance is operationally unlikely.

combinations.label: High amount + unusual billing pattern
combinations.why: A high amount combined with weekend or round-dollar billing is a stronger pattern than amount alone.

combinations.label: Several moderately unusual signals
combinations.why: Three or more utilization or billing signals are each moderately above the queue norm. No single one is alarming, but together they are unusual.

strong_indicators.label: Policy strong indicator: duplicate billing with service overlap
